cards.claim: Cubic5, Polar Express, and Muon-Jordan reach nearly indistinguishable final validation loss on GPT-2 Small
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small (NanoGPT), 3 random seeds, standard training setup
cards.effect: Final loss differences < 0.006 (cubic5: 3.623, Polar Express 4-step: 3.629, Muon-Jordan 4-step: 3.624, SVD: 3.623)
cards.evidence: Empirical ablation on GPT-2 Small comparing five orthogonalization variants across 1–5 steps
cards.quote: The gap among the strongest variants is very small: five-step cubic5 reaches 3.623, four-step Polar Express reaches 3.629, five-step Polar Express reaches 3.624, four-step Muon-Jordan reaches 3.624, and the explicit FP32 SVD polar factor also reaches 3.623. These runs differ by less than 0.006 final validation loss, while their numerical interpretation and matrix-multiplication costs are quite different.

cards.claim: Cubic5 uses 33% fewer dominant matrix multiplications than quintic Newton–Schulz per step
cards.conditions: Matrix operation count on rectangular matrices; bfloat16 arithmetic
cards.effect: 10 dominant multiplications (cubic5 5-step) vs 15 (quintic 5-step); roughly 1/3 wall-clock reduction for rectangular matrices
cards.evidence: Direct FLOP and matrix-multiplication count derivation
cards.quote: This schedule uses 10 dominant matrix multiplications, compared with 15 for five quintic iterations... For highly rectangular matrices, the rectangular multiplications dominate and the cubic schedule saves roughly one third of the dominant multiplications.

cards.claim: Exact FP32 SVD polar factor does not improve final validation loss over approximate Newton–Schulz methods
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small, comparison of SVD vs cubic5, Polar Express, Muon-Jordan across 1–5 steps
cards.effect: SVD converges to ~3.623 loss, matching best approximate methods; no quality gain from exact polar decomposition
cards.evidence: Empirical ablation showing SVD does not dominate approximate polynomial methods
cards.quote: exact SVD does not improve over the strongest approximate Newton–Schulz updates in our GPT-2 Small runs.

cards.claim: Training quality is governed by spectral transform shape, not polar decomposition accuracy alone
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small experiments with multiple orthogonalization polynomials; bfloat16 precision
cards.effect: Cubic5, Polar Express, Muon-Jordan all reach same loss region despite different spectral maps; SVD does not dominate
cards.evidence: Ablation and loss trajectory analysis showing non-monotone dependence on orthogonalization steps
cards.quote: This ablation suggests that optimizer quality is not determined solely by polar decomposition accuracy. If polar accuracy were the governing factor, the SVD baseline would be expected to dominate the approximate polynomial methods. Instead, training quality appears to depend on the effective spectral transform applied to the momentum update.

cards.claim: Cubic5 matches Muon-Jordan quintic within ~0.001 validation loss on hybrid MoE/Mamba models (1B–4B parameters)
cards.conditions: Nemotron-3-Nano hybrid MoE/Mamba scaling experiments (1B-A315M, 2B-A500M, 4B-A770M); bfloat16; WSD learning-rate schedule; 88B–215B token budgets
cards.effect: Validation loss differences: 1B: −0.0008, 2B: −0.0001, 4B: +0.001; PPL differences similarly small (< 0.004)
cards.evidence: End-to-end training experiments on three model scales with identical hyperparameters except orthogonalization method
cards.quote: cubic5 matches the Muon-Jordan quintic update within about 0.001 validation loss on hybrid MoE/Mamba models with one billion to four billion parameters.

cards.claim: Four-step Polar Express and four-step Muon-Jordan can reach good training quality despite differing scalar orthogonalization behavior
cards.conditions: GPT-2 Small, 1–5 orthogonalization steps, single seed shown with same pattern across 3 seeds
cards.effect: Both reach ~3.629–3.624 loss with 4 steps; further steps show non-monotone improvement
cards.evidence: Ablation showing truncated polynomial steps have non-monotone loss curves and can plateau early
cards.quote: Polar Express also improves with additional steps, reaching 3.629 at five steps. Muon-Jordan improves rapidly through four steps, from 3.676 to 3.624, and then slightly increases to 3.625 at five steps.

cards.claim: Cubic5 achieves relative training-loss parity with Muon-Jordan in early optimization phase but shows transient 2% relative difference early in training
cards.conditions: Nemotron-3-Nano 4B model; Megatron-LM; 215B token budget; bfloat16; WSD schedule
cards.effect: Early-phase relative difference ~2%, decays rapidly, then ~0 after initial phase; final loss indistinguishable
cards.evidence: Training-loss trajectory comparison (Figure 4) with relative-difference inset; final metrics in Table 4
cards.quote: The relative difference is largest (about 2%) at the beginning of training, but it decays rapidly and then fluctuates around zero for the remaining token budget. This pattern is consistent with a transient difference in the early optimization dynamics rather than a persistent shift in the training trajectory.
